report.summary: Reviewed chunk 6 of correctness.py: test extraction, task derivation, seeding, gate setup. Claims mostly match code; some docstring details uncheckable from this chunk.

handoff.purpose: Test function extraction, commit-based task derivation, measurement-based seeding, and correctness gate wiring.

symbols.name: _test_functions
symbols.note: Extracts test function names and source segments from a Python file using ast. Returns dict keyed by node id ('test_x' or 'ClassName::test_x'). Returns empty dict on non-.py, empty text, or SyntaxError.

symbols.name: derive_task_from_commit
symbols.note: Proposes a candidate correctness task from a commit's diff. Returns None if no test file changed or no f2p candidates. Builds overlay, f2p, p2p lists from test file changes.

symbols.name: seed_task_from_commit
symbols.note: Derives a candidate task and measures it in a disposable worktree. Returns (task, diagnostics) or (None, diagnostics). Measures before/after statuses, filters f2p/p2p, freezes selection, verifies before-state.

symbols.name: correctness_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate callable for TaskAttempt. Closes on unverified before-state or moved selection. Only defines the inner _gate, which is incomplete in this chunk.

claims.text: The key is the node id form pytest actually accepts -- ``test_x`` for a module-level function, ``ClassName::test_x`` for a method -- because the class qualifier is not optional and getting it wrong makes the node id ``missing``.
claims.why: The function produces keys exactly in that format: node.name for module-level, f"{node.name}::{child.name}" for methods.

claims.text: That is not a hypothetical: the first run of this seeder used unqualified names from ``structcore.extract_units`` (which reports a method as a bare ``test_alive_then_stale``) and the before-state check refuted 19 of 22 candidate nodes in one commit for exactly that reason.
claims.why: This chunk contains no historical record or reference to structcore.extract_units; the claim is anecdotal and cannot be verified from this code.

claims.text: ``ast`` rather than a regex or the structural extractor: it is stdlib, it is exact about nesting, and pytest node ids are a Python-only concept anyway.
claims.why: The function imports ast and uses ast.parse and ast.get_source_segment; no regex or external extractor is used.

claims.text: A file that does not parse contributes nothing (the caller then mints nothing from it) rather than contributing guesses.

The commit's own diff is the oracle, exactly as in ``mint.py``: what the commit ADDED or CHANGED in a test file is a FAIL_TO_PASS candidate, what it left untouched in the same file is a PASS_TO_PASS candidate, and the base is the commit's parent.
claims.why: The function compares after_units vs before_units; changed functions go to f2p, unchanged to p2p; base is parent revision.

claims.text: NOTHING here is trusted. Every derived node id is a CLAIM that :func:`verify_before_state` then tries to refute by running it on the base; a node id this function gets wrong (a test nested in a class, say, whose real node id carries the class) comes back ``missing`` and takes the task down with it.
claims.why: The docstring describes the intended flow; the function itself only proposes candidates. The verification is done in seed_task_from_commit and correctness_gate. The claim that wrong node ids come back missing is consistent with pytest behavior, but that specific outcome is not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` when the commit changed no test file -- a real and common case (``efd0ed6`` in this repo's own history is a fix with no test at all), reported by returning nothing rather than by inventing a label.
claims.why: The function returns None when no test file is changed or when no f2p candidates are found. The specific commit hash is uncheckable but the behavior matches.

claims.text: THE LISTS ARE MEASURED, NEVER CLAIMED. :func:`derive_task_from_commit` proposes node ids off the commit's diff; every one of them is a guess, and this function's whole job is to try to refute each guess by running it twice in one disposable worktree: base + test overlay -> the BEFORE statuses; base + test overlay + reference fix -> the AFTER statuses
claims.why: The function runs before_run and after_run in a disposable worktree with the described sequence.

claims.text: FAIL_TO_PASS  not passing BEFORE, passing AFTER, and TOUCHED by the commit (a test that was already red and that the commit never mentions is not this fix's witness)
claims.why: The filtering logic requires before_status not in PROVEN_NOT_PASSING (so not passing), after_status == STATUS_PASSED, and node in changed.

claims.text: PASS_TO_PASS  passing BEFORE and passing AFTER
claims.why: The condition `before_status == STATUS_PASSED and after_status == STATUS_PASSED` adds to p2p.

claims.text: Everything else is DROPPED WITH ITS REASON RECORDED on the task (``dropped_candidates``) -- never silently, because the drop rate is itself the measurement of how much a corpus is worth.
claims.why: The function records dropped nodes in diagnostics['dropped'] and then assigns task['dropped_candidates'] = diagnostics['dropped'].

claims.text: Real examples from this repo's own history, both found by running this rather than by reasoning: a test named ``..._still_...`` that the fix ADDED but which already passed on the base (demoted to the regression set), and an ``xfail``-marked test that is red before AND after the reference fix, so it can never witness anything (dropped).
claims.why: The specific examples are historical and not present in this chunk; the logic does handle those cases (a test that passes before is demoted, a test that fails before and after is dropped), so the described behavior is consistent, but the examples themselves cannot be verified.

claims.text: A task with no surviving FAIL_TO_PASS node is NOT admitted -- ``(None, diagnostics)`` with the reason. ``efd0ed6`` in this repo is such a commit: a real fix that shipped no test at all.
claims.why: The function returns (None, diagnostics) with reason when f2p is empty. The specific commit hash is uncheckable.

claims.text: Signature and return type match the attempt's gate contract exactly (``(RunnerContext) -> GateResult``), so wiring is ``TaskAttempt(..., gate=correctness_gate(task, repo_root))`` with no change to ``spine/`` at all.
claims.why: The inner _gate is defined as taking ctx and returning GateResult, but the full signature and the contract of TaskAttempt are in another module (daedalus.spine.attempt) not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: IT FAILS CLOSED ON AN UNVERIFIED TASK, and that is the point. The attempt's worktree already HAS the candidate's change in it by the time a gate runs, so the before-state cannot be measured there -- it has to have been measured earlier, against this exact base revision. A task with no verified before-state receipt for ``ctx.base_revision`` is REFUSED (``passed=False``) rather than evaluated, because a FAIL_TO_PASS list that was never shown to fail is precisely the vacuous green this module exists to prevent.
claims.why: The gate's inner _gate is cut off mid-definition; the verification of before-state and the refusal logic are not present in this chunk. The docstring describes the intended behavior, but the code to implement it is not visible.

claims.text: IT ALSO REFUSES A SELECTION THAT MOVED. The receipt records the digest of the selection it was measured under; this recomputes that digest from the task as presented and refuses on any mismatch. Widening the lists after the verification (say, to include a test the candidate itself added), narrowing them to drop an inconvenient one, or pointing them at a different base all change the digest and all get the same refusal. What was measured is what was declared, checkably.
claims.why: The digest-checking logic is not present in this chunk; the gate is incomplete here.

claims.text: What this gate adds over ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate``: pytest_gate asks "did the suite exit 0", which a candidate satisfies by changing nothing. This asks "did the previously-RED tests go GREEN, and did the previously-GREEN ones stay green" -- a question a no-op change cannot pass.
claims.why: The comparison to pytest_gate and the actual evaluation logic are not in this chunk; the gate is incomplete.

observations.what: The _test_functions function uses ast.get_source_segment which may return None for nodes without source; it falls back to ast.dump. This is a reasonable fallback.

In derive_task_from_commit, the `status` variable from _changed_files is only checked for 'D' prefix; other statuses like 'R' (rename) are treated as changed, which may be intended but could affect overlay inclusion.
The correctness_gate function's inner _gate is defined but not returned; the chunk ends mid-definition. This is a structural incompleteness, but likely resolved in the next chunk.
